eala.title: Alex Eala shares front row with Anna Wintour at New York Fashion Week show | ABS-CBN Entertainment
eala.description: Alex Eala joined Vogue’s Anna Wintour in the front row at the Michael Kors fashion show.
eala.text: Filipina tennis star Alex Eala was spotted seated in the front row beside Vogue’s Anna Wintour at the Michael Kors fashion show during New York Fashion Week. Television host Keltie Knight shared a clip on TikTok showing Alex sitting next to the renowned fashion editor at the event. “ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour,” Keltie wrote. Fans online were quick to react to the moment. “Wow! Alex with Anna Wintour.. 😳😳😳 Tennis star to fashionista ❤️,” one fan wrote. @keltieknight ICONIC ANNA sighting at @Michael Kors ✨ #NYFW #VOGUE #annawintour ♬ Danceteria - Madonna Anna previously shared how Alex caught her attention, particularly because of the young athlete’s growing interest in fashion and willingness to learn more about the industry. “We had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion. How she wants to learn about it and follow it and I think it’s great,” she said in an interview at the US Open. “It’s wonderful how sports and fashion have become this wonderful sort of marriage,” she added. Aside from the Michael Kors show, Alex also attended the fashion shows of Tory Burch and Calvin Klein during the New York Fashion Week. Tory Burch marked Alex's first event at NYFW. In an interview with Cultured Magazine, Alex reflected on the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. "Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she highlighted. At the Calvin Klein show, Alex also landed a front-row seat alongside several international stars, including Sadie Sink, Tate McRae, and Lingling Kwong. READ: Alex Eala attends her first New York Fashion Week event Prior to attending New York Fashion Week, Alex also appeared on the US national television program CBS Mornings. The 21-year-old tennis star also opened up about what the past year has taught her about the power of representation and how she hopes her journey can inspire others, particularly the younger generation. "One thing I’ve learned this past year is really the power of representation and how deep of an effect inspiration can have. When I interact with the people who support me and they tell me their stories, it really touches me," she said. "I just hope that whatever I do and the job that I have, and my day-to-day work inspires other people and inspires the youth especially to chase their dreams," she added. Filipino tennis superstar Alex Eala shared a bit of what she’s been feeling as she joined her first-ever New York Fashion Week. In a quick interview with American fashion magazine Vogue before the start of the Calvin Klein show, the WTA ranked number 18 expressed how it’s a different kind of New York she’s been experiencing. Alex was wearing an all-white attire with gloves during the event. Some of her fans shared on various social media platforms how gorgeous and beautiful the Filipino tennis superstar has been with her outfits. READ: Alex Eala attends her first New York Fashion Week event Quickly explaining her outfit for the show, Alex shared how it also pays homage to her Wimbledon experience as she also wore an all-white outfit then. “Yes, I love the all white. It’s very reminiscent of Wimbledon and I love the belt–– how it’s a black accent. I think it really stands out and my favorite part is the gloves. I love wearing gloves,” she expressed. When asked about her New York Fashion Week experience, the Filipino athlete had nothing but good words. She maintained how nervous she’s been but at the same time excited for the whole new experience. “This is my first New York Fashion Week so I feel like I’m getting a pretty authentic experience of rushing around with the traffic and fitting gym in as well. I’m really excited. I've been nervous but in a very good way,” she explained. Prior to the New York Fashion Week, Alex had a successful run at the US Open earlier this month where she was able to reach the Third Round of the tournament. She was defeated in a three-set battle with American player Iva Jovic. WHO SAID THIS: Alex Eala continues to soar higher It was also during the US Open wherein British media executive and former editor-in-chief of American Vogue Anna Wintour took notice of the fashion sense of Alex and how much the rising star is willing to learn more about it. “We had the young Filipino star, you know, you could see even in such a young star how interested she is in fashion. How she wants to learn about it and follow it and I think it’s great,” Anna previously expressed. Alex Eala continues her stint at New York Fashion Week as she attended the Calvin Klein fashion show. In an Instagram reel posted by Perfect Magazine, the Filipina tennis star was seated in the front row alongside several international stars including Sadie Sink, Tate McRae, and Lingling Kwong. Prior to the Calvin Klein show, Alex made her New York Fashion Week debut at the Tory Burch fashion show. In an interview with Cultured Magazine, the Filipina tennis star reflected on the similarities between sports and fashion, particularly when it comes to self-expression. "Sports and fashion are common in a way where you get to express yourself and you get to show your personality," she highlighted. Alex also playfully acknowledged that she is still discovering more about the fashion world. "Sports is very physically demanding and fashion... maybe come back to me after this week and I'll know more about it," she said. New York Fashion Week runs from September 10 to 15. According to NYFW.com, the event "provides leading designers from around the world with an unrivaled global platform to showcase their collections." Before making her New York Fashion Week debut, Alex also appeared on the US national television program CBS Mornings. During the interview, she was asked how she has been navigating her growing popularity and the attention that has come with her recent success. "I think step-by-step. I try to not to look so much at the bigger picture all time because I can get lost and it can get overwhelming with a lot of emotions especially with the support that I get," she said. READ: Alex Eala opens up on pressure, inspiration, representation When asked about the pressure of representing the Philippines on the international stage, Alex shared how she has learned to embrace high-pressure situations as part of being a competitive athlete. "It definitely comes with pressure. But the life of a competitive athlete comes with pressure and pressure is a privilege and I have never been able to relate something more and now when I face high pressure situations, I’m able to take it in my stride and especially with the experience I've been gaining this year, I look forward to being in those situations. So, this US Open has just been so great." Alex recently competed at the US Open, where she bowed out following a hard-fought match against familiar opponent American player Iva Jovic, 7-5, 3-6, 7-5. She is set to return to action at the WTA 500 Singapore Open, which will run from September 21 to 27. There are some amazing people in this room so I'm so happy to be a part of it," she remarked. Celebrity couple James Reid and Issa Pressman released their latest single, “On My Way”, on all digital streaming platforms. In her Instagram account, the singer-actress shared that it is a song that they composed together. “Our song together,” Issa wrote. “On My Way” is part of James’ latest album, Honey, I’m Home , which is a 10-track album released under Sony Music Entertainment. READ: Issa Pressman marks James Reid’s 33rd birthday: ‘With you I feel at home’ An official lyric visualizer was also released by James on his YouTube account which Issa hoped that fans can check out as well. The lyrics of the song showcased the love that the two have for each other and how the stars have aligned for them. “What if you've always been mine? What if the stars aligned. Way before the time when our eyes first met. And our hearts didn't know yet. We were meant to be together. In this lifetime and the next,” the first stanza of the song went. Apart from “On My Way”, James shared in an interview with ABS-CBN News how another song in his latest album is dedicated to his future child with Issa. “We mentioned that name (Indiana) one day and considered it for a baby name. Issa and I always talk about having a child. I thought, ‘Wow, we love this imaginary person who does not exist yet and is not even present. We love you even though you aren’t here.’ That love will be there even after we are gone,” he shared with ABS-CBN News earlier this month. READ: Issa Pressman on bashers: ‘I cannot control them’ Issa and James have been together for several years already and have expressed the love they have for each other. In a previous interview, James explained how Issa has been always there for him especially during the challenging times. “It was just love. I'd never had one single shadow of a doubt that it was her. No one ever made me feel the way I feel with her. And when she was going through that, I said, I don't know how I know this, but if you can get through this, you're going to be the strongest person I know. I said, 'You're going to be my greatest teacher. You're going to be the one that teaches me about love. You're going to be the one that teaches me about what it means to be strong, what it means to love, what it needs to be kind.' And funny enough, it has turned out that way,” he previously shared. Barbie Forteza opened up about her non-negotiable when it comes to love. PUSH ABS-CBN got to talk with Barbie during the exclusive block screening of her latest film Saving Cherry , organized by Avignon Clinic and Travertine Longevity Clinic on Saturday, September 12, at the EDSA Shangri-La Mall. In the film, Barbie plays Cherry, a woman whose husband cheats on her on their wedding night. With the topic of non-negotiables coming up in the film, PUSH ABS-CBN asked Barbie what hers is in real life. READ: Barbie Forteza takes on a sexy comedy for the first time: ‘In-unleash ko lang yung wild side ko’ “My non-negotiable? Basta ‘pag hindi nila napapadali ‘yung buhay ko. Basta ‘pag hindi ako natatrato ng tama, okay na yan. Sige, go ka na. Let go na kita,” she said. “Ako kasi, ako ‘yung tipo ng tao, ng babae, na alam ko na kaya ko naman pasayahin ‘yung sarili ko. Kaya ko mag-provide for myself. And so I guess, if I would be in a relationship, it is something I want to be in,” she said. She acknowledged that relationships require compromise, but emphasized that there are limits to what she is willing to accept. “And para sa akin, I would compromise, of course, kasi commitment ‘yun. But I will never settle.” Also starring in Saving Cherry are Mika Salamanca, AC Bonifacio, Sassa Gurl, and Mikee Quintos, who play Cherry’s close friends in the film. According to Barbie, their friendship continued even after they wrapped filming. She shared that they sometimes spend time together at Mikee’s home to catch up away from work. “Yes, we do. Sometimes after ng shoot or ng photoshoot, dumidiretso kami sa bahay ni Mikee. Tinutuloy namin doon ng chikahan. Kasi syempre sa work, di kami makapagchikahan, diba? So, mas ‘yun. Basta we always make sure na meron kaming time together outside work,” she said. Barbie also talked about the dynamic among the group, noting how each of her co-stars brings a different personality and energy to their friendship. “Iba-iba eh. Iba-iba sila ng ugali. Iba-iba sila ng level of energy. Lalo si AC, siya ‘yung may pinakamataas na energy kasi siya yung pinakabata sa amin,” she said. She described Mikee as the one who brings wisdom to the group, while Sassa is known for her witty one-liners. “I guess, ‘yung wisdom ay ‘yung manggagaling kay Mikee. And ‘yung mga one-liner na sobrang nakakapagpatawa sa aming lahat, si Sassa.” Meanwhile, Barbie said Mika brings grace and support to their group. “And ‘yung grace and ‘yung support nanggagaling kay Mika. So, ang ganda. Ang ganda ng dynamic naming magkakaibigan kasi todo supporta sa isa't isa. Iniintindi ‘yung amats ng bawat isa.” Saving Cherry is currently showing in cinemas nationwide.

deped.title: Are K-12 grads ready for work, adult life? DepEd eyes longer OJT
deped.description: Education Secretary Sonny Angara said DepEd is looking to increase the amount of on-the-job training (OJT) for senior high school students to 640 hours, from the current 80 to 160 hours.
deped.text:
The Department of Education (DepEd) says there is still work to be done, citing feedback from employers who find some senior high school graduates not yet sufficiently prepared for the workplace.

Education Secretary Sonny Angara said DepEd is looking to increase the amount of on-the-job training (OJT) for senior high school students to 640 hours, from the current 80 to 160 hours.

Angara made the statement during the House Committee on Appropriations hearing on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget after Representative Brian Raymund Yamsuan asked whether K-12 graduates were adequately prepared for adult life.

“Kasi ’yun ang feedback namin from many employers na parang yung attitude ng mga hinahire nilang senior high graduates ay parang hilaw pa at parang hindi sanay sa eight-hour work day yung ating mga graduates.”

(That’s the feedback we’ve received from many employers—that the senior high graduates they hire seem to still be unprepared and are not yet accustomed to an eight-hour workday.)

With this, Angara said one of DepEd’s interventions is to increase the time learners spend in actual workplaces.

“So some of the interventions, aligned also na rin sa instruction ng ating mahal na Pangulo, is to increase the on-the-job training, or the number of hours spent in workplaces," he said.

(So some of the interventions, also aligned with the instruction of our President, are to increase on-the-job training, or the number of hours spent in workplaces.)

“So doon sa mga employers, to any industries to absorb ang learners na po natin, ay ang goal natin is umakyat sa 640 hours of on-the-job training, kumpara doon sa ngayon 80 to 160," Angara added.

(So for employers, for any industries that will absorb our learners, our goal is to increase [the requirement] to 640 hours of on-the-job training, compared with the current 80 to 160.)

Angara noted that some employers already provide as much as 500 hours, but consultations with industry groups showed that employers wanted longer workplace exposure to assess students’ fitness for work and help develop their skills.

He added that longer OJT could also improve graduates’ chances of being hired by the same employers who trained them.

“At ang kagandahan niyan, pag nakilala na ho talaga ng employer, mas malaki na ho yung chance na siya ay ma-hire pagka-graduate niya dahil nag-invest na rin sa training yung employer na nag-employ sa kanya as an on-the-job trainee," he said.

(And the good thing about that is that once the employer really gets to know the student, there is a greater chance that the student will be hired after graduation because the employer has already invested in the training of the person they employed as an on-the-job trainee.)

‘Life skills’ for work, college, entrepreneurship

But DepEd’s response goes beyond workplace exposure. Angara said the curriculum is also being changed to include a new subject on life skills, which he said is intended to prepare students for different paths after senior high school—whether employment, entrepreneurship, or college.

“So it’s not just a purely academic subject, but also anything that we believe would make that person a good employee, or a good entrepreneur, or a good college student, whatever path he chooses to pursue after," he said.

(So it’s not just a purely academic subject, but also anything that we believe would make that person a good employee, a good entrepreneur, or a good college student, whatever path they choose to pursue afterward.)

The subject would include lessons on growth mindset, among other skills that Angara said are not normally taught in the formal curriculum.

He cited a survey of students that, according to him, showed an overwhelming majority did not believe education would make their lives better.

“So wala pong growth mindset sa kanila. So we’re trying to change that because alam naman natin all over the world education is key to a person’s success, di ba?" he said.

(So they don’t have a growth mindset. So we’re trying to change that because we know that all over the world, education is key to a person’s success, right?)

Angara said DepEd also wants to incorporate future skills and some AI-related learning as the workplace continues to change.

“Also a little bit of AI, a little bit of, because that’s the way of the future, a little bit of future skills also, whatever.”

(Also a little bit of AI, because that’s the way of the future, and a little bit of future skills as well.)

He described the curriculum as evolving according to what tomorrow’s workplace will require.

“So it’s a changing curriculum in the sense, or a changing subject, whatever the workplace of tomorrow will demand," he said.

On Monday, DepEd presented a P975.96-billion proposed budget for fiscal year 2027, including allocations for its attached agencies, before the House Committee on Appropriations, according to the department’s press release. It is appealing for an additional P145.19 billion for critical DepEd programs not funded under the 2027 National Expenditure Program.

DepEd’s FY 2027 NEP presentation includes P2.4 billion for 50,337 laptops for teachers, P1.12 billion for internet subscription renewal for 14,261 schools, and P2.25 billion for ICT solutions and capacity building.—LDF GMA News

rene.title: ‘PARA KAY RENE’: UST dedicates UAAP Season 89 campaign to Baterbonia family | ABS-CBN Sports
rene.description: Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family f
rene.text: University of Santo Tomas head coach Pido Jarencio (left) and the Baterbonia family in UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball. UAAP Media. MANILA — Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family found solace as they continue to cope with their loss. Rene’s parents, Rovelyn Baterbonia and Rene Baterbonia Sr., were present at the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball matches on Wednesday and visited UST ahead of its game against De La Salle University. Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene. “Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle. “Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. Niyakap, umiiyak yung nanay.” The Baterbonias were already in attendance at the Mall of Asia Arena earlier in the day as Ateneo de Manila University — the school that had committed to Rene well before the June 8 tragedy in Dipaculao, Aurora — dominated University of the East, 101-74. However, before the UST-La Salle match, the Baterbonias moved from the lower box section to the seats behind the Tigers’ bench. It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout. “Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio. “Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.” After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family. “Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio. “Every game is dedicated kay Rene Baterbonia. We’re not from Ateneo, basta kami, sarili namin, sa puso namin nanggaling yun,” he added. The Ateneo Blue Eagles have also dedicated their campaign to the Baterbonia and Adili families, with the players donning jerseys bearing patches of their initials, “DA | RB.” The parents of Divine Adili, Elias and Ifeoma, were also in attendance during the Ateneo-UE match. moira.title: Moira dela Torre hits 11 million followers on Spotify | ABS-CBN Entertainment
moira.description: OPM singer-songwriter Moira dela Torre now has 11 million followers on music streaming platform Spotify.
moira.text: MANILA -- OPM singer-songwriter Moira dela Torre now has 11 million followers on music streaming platform Spotify. The "Tagpuan" hitmaker shared the newest milestone as "the most-followed Filipino soloist" on the platform via a social media post over the weekend. Dela Torre also known for her hits like "Malaya," "Paubaya," "Ikaw At Aiko," "Before It Sinks In" is currently gearing up for her fourth major concert billed as "Where It All Started" happening on October 4 at 8 p.m. at the Mall of Asia Arena. In her upcoming concert, apart from her hits, she is set to share direct personal disclosures on stage. Joining her in her concert as guests are Ogie Alcasid, Adie, Johnoy Danao, December Avenue, and surprise co-billing artists. Tickets are still available in other sections via ticketmaster.ph Moira dela Torre to stage major concert at MOA Arena

vera.title: FACT CHECK: Romeo Poquiz did NOT make viral statement vs Marcoses
vera.description: At least two Facebook posts are claiming that retired Philippine Air Force Maj. Gen. Romeo Poquiz made a statement against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos. This is fake.
vera.text: Maj. Gen. Romeo Poquiz criticized Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, Louise “Liza” Araneta-Marcos. The old post came out on the Facebook page of Philippine Army Col. Audie Mongao, not Poquiz, on Jan, 6. There is no record of Poquiz making such a statement, even as he supported Mongao’s sentiment. At least two Facebook posts falsely attributed a viral statement to retired Air Force Maj. Gen. Romeo Poquiz denouncing the leadership of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos claiming they no longer have a mandate to lead. This is fake. VERA Files traced the earliest publicly available copy of the claim to a Sept. 6 post by an FB user. The graphic contains a photo of Poquiz and this fake quote attributed to him: “Hindi sobra na, kundi sobra sobra na. So, ano na? Liza at BBM, wala na kayong saysay sa Pilipinas para manatili pa. Hindi niyo pagmamay-ari ang Pilipinas. Tama na… (It’s not just too much anymore, it’s way, way too much. So, what now? Liza and BBM, there is no reason for you to stay in power. You do not own the Philippines. Enough is enough…).” The post also carried a caption that reads: “Ang Pilipinas ay hindi pag-aari ng isang pamilya, partido, o sinumang nakaupo sa kapangyarihan. Ito ay tahanan at kinabukasan ng bawat Pilipino. Kung may mga lider na nawawalan ng tiwala ng mamamayan, karapatan nating manawagan ng katapatan, transparency, pananagutan, at mabuting pamamahala. Ang tunay na lider ay hindi dapat kumapit sa kapangyarihan para sa pansariling interes, kundi magsilbi nang buong puso sa bayan. Hindi galit ang kailangan ng Pilipinas—kundi katotohanan, hustisya, pagkakaisa, at tapang na manindigan para sa tama. Ang kapangyarihan ay pansamantala; ang bayan ang permanente. ❤️ (The Philippines does not belong to one family, one political party, or anyone currently in power. It is the home and future of every Filipino. If there are leaders who have lost the trust of the people, we have the right to demand honesty, transparency, accountability, and good governance. A true leader should not cling to power for personal interest, but should serve the nation wholeheartedly. What the Philippines needs is not anger—but truth, justice, unity, and the courage to stand up for what is right. Power is temporary; the nation is permanent. )” A similar post was published on Sept. 6 and 7, bearing the same caption and graphic card. Contrary to what the post is implying, there are no records of Poquiz making this statement. The phrase “Sobra na, tama na!” was in the Jan. 6 Facebook post of Army Col. Audie A. Mongao, as he withdrew his “personal support” for the president and was subsequently put on floating status. Part of his post read: “Sobra na, tama na! The Filipino people are worth fighting for.” The fake posts surfaced amid renewed attention to Vice President Sara Duterte’s statements involving the Armed Forces of the Philippines on Sept. 7. Posted by two Facebook users, the posts have so far collectively garnered 4,621 reactions, 1,106 comments, and 996 shares.
